Behavior implemented (traced to behavior-model.txt IDs):
- BEH-001/BEH-002/BEH-003: artifact present iff Android project detected AND >=1 supported declaration; absent otherwise; gate implemented as the first line of buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject().
- BEH-004/BEH-005: no command/navigation-artifact behavior touched.
- BEH-006/BEH-007: per-file scan over roledSymbolIndex.files (language==='kotlin'), brace-depth + comment/string-stripped line scanning.
- BEH-008/BEH-009: exact-annotation-gated extraction (COMPOSABLE_ANNOTATION_PATTERN/PREVIEW_ANNOTATION_PATTERN), never name-based.
- BEH-010/INV-003: child-call resolution is same-file exact-name-match only (resolveChildCalls); 0 matches silently omitted, >1 matches produce a warning, never a guess.
- BEH-011: extractStructuralRegionCalls recognizes the 7 fixed names via both call-with-parens and trailing-lambda-only syntax (a real bug caught and fixed during manual smoke verification — see "Deviations" below).
- BEH-012: false positives from comments/strings/anonymous-lambdas/higher-order-returned-composables/class-members all verified absent via both manual smoke testing and the automated test suite.
- BEH-013: deterministic source ranges via findBodyBoundary/findMatchingBrace/findExpressionBodyEnd; annotation-start-to-body-close.
- BEH-014: finishIndexBuild() wiring (managedArtifacts/writeIndexManifest/runIndexCommand/android-index barrel).
- BEH-015: no new cache/fingerprint; verified via checkPartialRebuildEligibility inspection and empirically via 4 incremental-regression integration tests (add/change/remove/no-op).

Pseudocode sections implemented: PSE-001 through PSE-025 (androidComposeTypes.ts implements PSE-001..PSE-011; buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts implements PSE-012..PSE-020; managedArtifacts.ts/writeIndexManifest.ts/runIndexCommand.ts/android/index.ts implement PSE-021..PSE-024; PSE-025's manifestTypes.ts no-change conclusion confirmed and left unmodified).

Assumptions preserved:
- Compose scanning gates on androidProject.detected (behavior-model.txt's resolved "Unresolved design question", by direct precedent from buildComposeNavigationRoutes.ts).
- Same-file-only child-call resolution (pseudocode-packet.txt's documented scope-narrowing guard).
- No manifestTypes.ts change (confirmed, not just assumed, via direct source retrieval this stage).

Assumptions removed or guarded:
- Pseudocode's PSE-013 "only depth-0 and depth-1-directly-inside" restriction on function-local nesting was loosened during implementation to "innermost enclosing function via textual containment" (any nesting depth within a function's body, not just immediate-child), since the fixed external contract's own Section 2.3 does not impose a maximum-nesting-depth restriction — the tighter restriction was pseudocode-packet.txt's own invented bound, not a fixed-contract requirement, and the looser rule is simpler, well-defined, and still correctly rejects class/object-body nesting (TST-014) because only `fun` boundaries are tracked as valid enclosing constructs. Documented here as a deviation (see below), not silently changed.

Deviations from the PseudocodePacket, with reason:
1. PSE-013's exact scope-classification algorithm (line-by-line brace-depth-stack with live frame buffering) was replaced during implementation with a whole-file-text char-index approach (matchAll + findMatchingParen/findMatchingBrace/findEnclosingFunction-by-textual-containment), matching buildComposeNavigationRoutes.ts's own established technique more directly. Reason: the frame-buffering design sketched in pseudocode was substantially more complex to implement correctly (multi-line signature accumulation, simultaneous multi-frame body buffering) for no behavioral benefit over the simpler containment-search approach, which produces identical, easily-verified results and is the same pattern this repository already trusts for Compose-adjacent scanning.
2. The function-local nesting-depth restriction was loosened, as described above under "Assumptions removed or guarded."
3. CALL_CANDIDATE_PATTERN and the structural-region regex were both widened, after manual smoke testing surfaced a real bug, to match trailing-lambda-only invocation syntax (`Identifier { }`, no parens) in addition to `Identifier(...)` — real Compose code almost universally calls `Scaffold`/`Column`/`Row`/`Box`/`LazyColumn`/`LazyRow` via trailing-lambda-only syntax, and the pseudocode's implicit parens-only assumption would have silently produced near-empty structural-region output on real-world code. Caught before any test was written, via the manual smoke script described in the retrieval report.

Blockers encountered:
- The implementation-context automated readiness gate (CONTEXT_ADEQUACY_INSUFFICIENT), resolved via explicit user authorization as described in the context-gate override notice above. No other blocker was encountered; no forbidden-edit-area conflict arose; no scope-expansion was required.

Unresolved risks:
- Multi-line triple-quoted Kotlin strings (`"""..."""`) are not string-literal-stripped by this batch's conservative scanner (only single-line `"..."` strings are blanked) — a `@Composable`-looking or brace-perturbing text fragment inside a triple-quoted string could theoretically still produce a false positive or depth-tracking error. Documented as a known, accepted limitation consistent with the base Kotlin adapter's own documented conservative-parser limitations; not covered by a fixture in this batch.
- The `<...>` generic-bracket skip in findBodyBoundary/splitTopLevelByComma/findTopLevelChar could misclassify a `<`/`>` used as a comparison operator in a default-parameter-value expression as a generic bracket, in the rare case such an expression appears in a Compose function's parameter list. Low real-world likelihood; not covered by a fixture in this batch.
- Local classes declared inside a function body (rare Kotlin pattern) are not tracked as a nesting boundary separate from their enclosing function, so a composable member of such a local class could be incorrectly classified as function-local rather than correctly rejected as an unsupported member. Documented in pseudocode-packet.txt's "Assumptions removed or guarded" section as an accepted edge case.
